summary: Addresses acronym and expansion extraction from scientific PDFs, where regex alone misses expansions and GPT-4 alone misidentifies acronyms. The method preprocesses text, uses regex to find acronyms, and sends short surrounding windows to GPT-4 for expansions. The authors report that neither component performs well alone, and that GPT-4 output can vary between runs.
short_summary: Combines regex preprocessing with GPT-4 over short text windows to extract acronym-expansion pairs from papers.
rq_relation: RQ2: example of a regex-then-LLM cascade for scientific text; not about gaps

summary: Addresses limited context windows and shallow answers when LLMs search scientific literature for query-specific knowledge. WISE uses a tree-based LLM workflow that extracts, refines, and ranks non-redundant content, with adaptive stopping. On HBB gene-disease experiments it cuts processed text by over 80 percent and reports higher recall than search engines and LLM baselines.
short_summary: Tree-structured LLM workflow extracts and ranks query-relevant knowledge from papers, reducing processed text by over 80 percent.
rq_relation: RQ3: staged reduction of long-document input to fit a limited LLM budget

summary: Addresses under-reported limitations in scientific papers that reviewers often miss. Tree-of-Concerns runs five category-specific skeptic personas as parallel debate trees, followed by a Panel Review that re-checks each surviving claim. Evaluated single-paper without retrieval on ToC-Bench (414 papers, 1,905 unstated limitations), it improves precision by 79 percent and coverage by 11 percent over the strongest baseline.
short_summary: Multi-agent skeptic personas with panel review extract unstated limitations from single papers, evaluated on a 414-paper benchmark.
rq_relation: RQ1: LLM method and benchmark for detecting unstated limitations in full papers

summary: Asks whether LLMs can link scientific claims to supporting evidence across full-length papers, a deeper comprehension test than extraction alone. The authors compare three divide-and-conquer strategies across six LLMs on over 300 claim-evidence pairs in several domains. Closed models outperform open ones, and three-pass and one-by-one prompting improve linking at higher computational cost.
short_summary: Benchmark comparing three divide-and-conquer prompting strategies across six LLMs for linking claims to evidence in full papers.
rq_relation: RQ3: divide-and-conquer versus whole-paper prompting on full papers; cost trade-off informs RQ2

summary: Addresses scaling literature reviews over large corpora by fine-tuning open LLMs with error-focused human correction. The framework is applied to over 20,000 human migration articles to select relevant studies, trace trends, and identify research gaps. The authors find the literature overrepresents some environmental hazards while neglecting pollution and infectious disease effects.
short_summary: Fine-tunes open LLMs with error-focused human validation to screen 20,000 migration papers and identify research gaps.
rq_relation: RQ1: LLM-assisted literature-level gap mapping over a large corpus in one field

summary: Addresses the high cost of per-row LLM calls in semantic SQL by routing most rows through a fast proxy and uncertain cases to an LLM oracle. SUPG-IT extends SUPG to streaming execution with joint precision and recall guarantees, and GAMCAL calibrates proxy scores with a monotone GAM under a single cost-error tradeoff. On six benchmarks both reach F1 of at least 0.95, and GAMCAL uses up to 58 percent fewer oracle calls than LOTUS.
short_summary: Streaming model cascades route semantic SQL rows between a proxy and an LLM oracle, with precision and recall guarantees and fewer oracle calls.
rq_relation: RQ2: cascade routing with guarantees and oracle-call savings against full LLM inference

summary: Addresses the storage and annotation cost of downloading candidate videos for dataset construction by using LLMs to pre-screen metadata first. The LLM filter is checked against a four-annotator majority vote using Gwet's AC1 agreement and compared with two keyword heuristics. The authors also report cost comparisons and make their implementation available on GitHub.
short_summary: Uses LLMs to pre-screen video metadata before downloads, reducing storage and annotation costs for dataset construction.
rq_relation: RQ2: LLM metadata pre-filter as a cost-saving gate; video domain, not scientific text

summary: Addresses LLM cost in multi-party conversation processing by filtering snippets before they reach the LLM. Knowledge distilled from LLMs is used to annotate a synthetic multi-party dataset, which fine-tunes MobileBERT for multi-label intent classification. Only relevant snippets are forwarded, and the cost reduction depends on the intents and data distribution.
short_summary: Distills an LLM into a MobileBERT intent filter that passes only relevant conversation snippets to the LLM, cutting cost.
rq_relation: RQ2: small distilled classifier as a pre-LLM filter; conversational domain

summary: Addresses the GPU cost of deploying multimodal LLMs online for video quality classification. An entropy-based lightweight model estimates uncertainty and forwards only high-uncertainty cases to the MLLM for final evaluation. Deployed on a short-video platform, it reduces inappropriate-content view rate by 9.9 percent in an online A/B test without hurting engagement.
short_summary: Cascade where a lightweight entropy-based filter selects uncertain video cases for a multimodal LLM, cutting GPU usage.
rq_relation: RQ2: entropy-gated small-model cascade before an MLLM, with production A/B evidence

summary: Addresses the scarcity of machine-readable thermoelectric data by extracting properties from full-text articles with LLM agents. The pipeline combines dynamic token allocation, zero-shot multi-agent extraction, and conditional table parsing, benchmarked on 50 curated papers. GPT-4.1 scores highest, GPT-4.1 Mini is nearly as accurate at a fraction of the cost, and the pipeline yields a 27,822-record dataset.
short_summary: Agentic LLM workflow extracts thermoelectric properties from 10,000 full-text articles, comparing GPT-4.1 and Mini accuracy and cost.
rq_relation: RQ2: model-size cost-accuracy comparison for full-text extraction; background for RQ3

summary: Addresses clinical LLM deployment under privacy rules and limited GPUs, where small models struggle with long unstructured EHR notes. Regex and RAG pre-filtering highlight key information before a small local LLM extracts annotations. On an in-house head and neck cancer cohort and MIMIC-IV it improves the sensitivity, specificity and F1 of small models, and it is compared with fine-tuned LLMs.
short_summary: Regex and RAG pre-filtering of long clinical notes lets small local LLMs extract EHR annotations with better sensitivity and F1.
rq_relation: RQ2/RQ3: prefiltering lifts small LLMs on long documents; cost and privacy rationale

summary: Addresses limited human-coded data for open-response assessment by mixing human-coded and GPT-4o synthetic samples to fine-tune a BERT classifier. Three experiments vary synthetic sample size, variety and temperature. Best results come at an 80 percent synthetic ratio, lower temperature gives more stable gains, and filtering inconsistent synthetic samples does not help.
short_summary: Combines human-coded and LLM-synthetic data to fine-tune a BERT classifier for open-response assessment, varying augmentation ratios and temperatures.
rq_relation: Background only: LLM-generated labels distilled into a small classifier; not gap-related

summary: Addresses the trade-off between diversity and accuracy in LLM-generated text data. Logit suppression and temperature sampling raise diversity but reduce accuracy. Human label replacement raises the accuracy of models trained on diversified data by 14.4 percent in oracle studies, while out-of-scope filtering does not help.
short_summary: Studies diversity versus accuracy in LLM-generated training data, with human label replacement and out-of-scope filtering interventions.
rq_relation: Background only: human-in-the-loop LLM data generation; not gap mining

summary: Addresses choosing an approach for structured field extraction from business documents, where accuracy-only benchmarks give little guidance. Eleven systems, including commercial, reasoning, open-source and fine-tuned VLMs plus an OCR-regex floor, are scored on 750 synthetic documents. A selection framework maps task profiles to approaches through filtering and total-cost minimization.
short_summary: Benchmarks VLMs and an OCR baseline for structured field extraction from templated documents, with a cost-aware selection framework.
rq_relation: RQ2: cost and accuracy trade-offs across approaches, but on non-scientific documents

summary: Addresses weak long-context evaluation, since prior benchmarks were short, outdated, or focused on short dependencies. LooGLE provides post-2022 documents over 24,000 tokens, with 6,000 generated questions and over 1,100 human-written long-dependency QA pairs. Eight LLMs handle short dependencies well but struggle with long-dependency tasks, and retrieval helps short QA most.
short_summary: Introduces LooGLE, a long-document benchmark showing LLMs struggle with long-dependency QA despite strong short-dependency performance.
rq_relation: RQ3: general long-context QA benchmark; falls under the general-benchmark exclusion for extraction

summary: Addresses degraded use of information spread across multiple documents in long contexts, where both position and spacing matter. Multi-hop QA experiments show performance falls with distance from the context edges and between necessary pieces. Mitigations reduce superfluous content through knowledge-graph triple extraction and summarization, plus chain-of-thought prompting.
short_summary: Shows multi-hop QA degrades with information position and spacing in long contexts, and tests triple extraction and summarization fixes.
rq_relation: RQ3: degradation when evidence is spread out; triple extraction reduces input length

summary: Asks how well language models use relevant information at different positions in long inputs. Using multi-document QA and key-value retrieval, the authors show accuracy is highest when the relevant information is at the start or end and drops significantly mid-context. The degradation holds even for explicitly long-context models.
short_summary: Shows LLM accuracy drops when relevant information sits mid-context, using multi-document QA and key-value retrieval tests.
rq_relation: RQ3: seminal evidence of position-dependent degradation in long contexts

summary: Addresses lost-in-the-middle and distraction in long-context LLMs for multi-document QA. FltLM integrates a context filter with a soft mask that excludes irrelevant content within a single forward pass. The paper reports it outperforms supervised fine-tuning and retrieval-based methods on complex QA.
short_summary: Proposes FltLM, a long-context LLM with a soft-mask context filter that excludes irrelevant content for multi-document QA.
rq_relation: RQ3: in-model context filter as a mitigation; analogous to filter-then-answer

summary: Asks whether longer context improves RAG accuracy. The authors run RAG workflows on 20 open and commercial LLMs, varying context from 2,000 to 128,000 tokens (up to 2 million where possible) across three domain datasets. Few models keep consistent accuracy above 64k tokens, and the authors report distinct long-context failure modes.
short_summary: Studies how increasing context length affects RAG accuracy across 20 LLMs, finding few models stay accurate beyond 64k tokens.
rq_relation: RQ3: retrieval plus long context degrades for most models; direct evidence for RQ3 comparison

summary: Addresses lost-in-the-middle, where accuracy falls when the correct information lies mid-context. Attention-strengthening multi-document QA tasks train the model to focus on the desired information. The authors report absolute gains of 13.7 percent in shuffled multi-doc QA and 21.5 percent in passage retrieval, and release the Ziya-Reader model.
short_summary: Ziya-Reader uses position-agnostic decompositional training to improve multi-document QA accuracy over long contexts.
rq_relation: RQ3: training-based mitigation for lost-in-the-middle; not extraction-specific

summary: Addresses quality loss in LLMs even within their stated context limits during long-context retrieval. The authors find that specific attention heads correlate with retrieval scores, and a learned mechanism uses generated data to emphasize them. The method improves retrieval across tasks and models and combines with training-free context extension.
short_summary: Scales attention heads correlated with retrieval to improve LLM long-context retrieval quality, using a learned emphasis mechanism.
rq_relation: RQ3: attention-based mitigation for long-context retrieval; mechanistic

summary: Addresses LLMs failing to reason over sparse evidence in long contexts, where they often hallucinate retrieved facts. ALR2 aligns LLMs with an explicit two-stage procedure covering both retrieval and reasoning. It outperforms competitive baselines on long-context HotpotQA and SQuAD variants, with EM gains of at least 8.4 and 7.9.
short_summary: ALR2 aligns LLMs for an explicit retrieval step followed by reasoning, improving long-context QA on HotpotQA and SQuAD variants.
rq_relation: RQ3: retrieve-then-reason versus long-context prompting on QA benchmarks

summary: Addresses LLM failures on numeric reasoning over long contexts, where chain-of-thought prompting is costly in output tokens. The workflow decomposes tasks into judging, extraction, code-based processing, and conclusion, using smaller models for the simpler subtasks and LLM-generated code for calculations. On two numeric long-context benchmarks it improves accuracy and significantly reduces API cost.
short_summary: Decomposes numeric long-context tasks into judging, extraction, and code-based processing, using smaller models to cut API cost.
rq_relation: RQ2/RQ3: small-model decomposition cuts cost on long documents; code offloads calculation

summary: Addresses LLMs failing to use evidence already present in long inputs. ReContext is a training-free method that uses model-internal relevance signals to build a query-conditioned evidence pool and replays it before generation, keeping the full context. Experiments on eight 128K-token datasets with Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B and Llama3-8B show improved evidence utilization.
short_summary: ReContext replays query-conditioned evidence pools before generation, improving evidence utilization across Qwen3 and Llama3 on long contexts.
rq_relation: RQ3: training-free mitigation for evidence use in long contexts; recent preprint

summary: Addresses long-context QA, where long-context LLMs suffer lost-in-the-middle and chunked RAG loses global information. LongRAG combines global and factual retrieval perspectives in a plug-and-play RAG paradigm. On three multi-hop datasets it beats long-context LLMs by 6.94 percent, advanced RAG by 6.16 percent, and vanilla RAG by 17.25 percent.
short_summary: LongRAG combines global and factual retrieval views to outperform long-context LLMs and vanilla RAG on multi-hop QA.
rq_relation: RQ3: retrieval-based alternative to long-context prompting on multi-hop QA

summary: Challenges the claim that long-context LLMs make RAG obsolete for long-document QA. OP-RAG preserves the original chunk order when retrieving, and answer quality rises and then falls as more chunks are added, forming an inverted U. The sweet points reach higher quality with far fewer tokens than full-context input on public benchmarks.
short_summary: OP-RAG preserves chunk order and finds an inverted-U accuracy curve, reaching higher quality with fewer tokens than full-context input.
rq_relation: RQ3: order-preserving RAG versus full long-context input, with token-cost evidence

summary: Asks how transformers retrieve information from arbitrary positions in long contexts. Across models, a sparse set of attention heads, under five percent, act as retrieval heads that are universal, present already in short-context pretraining, and causally needed for retrieval. Masking them impairs chain-of-thought reasoning more than direct answering, with implications for hallucination and KV cache compression.
short_summary: Identifies sparse retrieval attention heads that are universal, causal for retrieval, and influence chain-of-thought reasoning.
rq_relation: RQ3: mechanistic account of long-context retrieval; background for degradation analysis

summary: Asks whether long-context processing can be moved from latent attention into executable interactions. Frontier coding agents organize text in file systems and use native tools for long-context reasoning, RAG, and open-domain QA over corpora of up to three trillion tokens. They outperform published state-of-the-art by 17.3 percent on average, which the authors attribute to tool proficiency and file-system navigation.
short_summary: Shows frontier coding agents with file-system tools outperform published long-context baselines on large-corpus QA and RAG benchmarks.
rq_relation: RQ3: agentic file-system alternative to semantic search and context-window scaling
